math_result.reasoning: Noise-corrected RSA estimator (eq 11): the quantity is an estimator (denoted by '~') of the inter-animal representational similarity, formed as the observed cross-animal RSA divided by the square root of the product of the two animals' Spearman-Brown-corrected split-half reliabilities. This matches the standard attenuation-correction structure r_corrected = r_observed / sqrt(rel_A * rel_B). The one subtlety is whether the Spearman-Brown (full-length) reliability correction belongs in the denominator when the numerator itself is computed on half-split data; the paper's text ('correlations of observations from half the trials of the same underlying process to itself (unlike the numerator)') does not fully pin down the numerator's trial usage, and with an informal '~' estimator this methodological choice cannot be demonstrated to be a definite algebraic error from the snippet alone. noncomputable def spearmanBrown (r : ℝ) : ℝ := 2 * r / (1 + r)

theorem spearman_brown_range {r : ℝ} (hr0 : 0 ≤ r) (hr1 : r < 1) : 0 ≤ spearmanBrown r ∧ spearmanBrown r < 1

summary: The paper's mathematical content (Appendix A2 model definitions and A4 evaluation formulas) was extracted into 12 EQUATION snippets: the 10 UGRNN/IntersectionRNN update-rule equations, the noise-corrected RSA estimator (eq 11), and the Spearman-Brown correction formula. Four snippets with non-trivial formal content were routed to verify-math-lean and all four PASSED machine-checked proofs: (i) the UGRNN state update (eq 3) is a convex combination of old state and candidate; (ii) the IntersectionRNN state update (eq 9) is likewise a convex combination; (iii) the IntersectionRNN output (eq 10) is a gated interpolation between raw input and ReLU candidate; (iv) the Spearman-Brown map r ↦ 2r/(1+r) is strictly increasing on (-1,1) and maps [0,1) into [0,1), so it is a coherent correlation correction. The remaining eight snippets were reviewed informally: the candidate/gate activation definitions are structurally sound with no algebraic, sign, or domain errors, and the RSA estimator matches the standard attenuation-correction form (its '~' estimator status and under-specified split-halving procedure preclude a confident error claim). No Lean result FAILED, so no fallback informal reviews were needed; the informal and formal verdicts agree everywhere. No findings at confidence ≥ 0.7; verdict NO_ERRORS. Two caveats. (1) The shared Lean project MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper pre-existed on disk (it already held proofs from an earlier, different verification run) and was reused, so per the verifier's deletion rules it was not deleted; lean_project_kept is true. (2) The following numeric/experimental inconsistencies are outside the mathematical-snippet scope and are flagged for the cross-section/statistical verifiers rather than this report: the appendix reports a maximum inter-animal consistency of 1.34, which is impossible for a Pearson correlation (the main text reports 0.34); A1 Table 1's stated relation 'total sweeps = number of augmentation combinations × 9981 objects' is not satisfied by the dataset-(1) total (16 augmentation combinations × 9981 = 159,696 ≠ 316,192); and the task-performance-vs-neural-fit correlation is reported as r = 0.59 in the text (Fig. 5b) but as r = 0.60 in the Fig. 5 caption.
